newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Thousands greet Nobel laureate on return to Timor.
newsitem.headline: Thousands greet Nobel laureate on return to Timor.

text.p: Tens of thousands of people greeted Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo on Tuesday when he returned to East Timor from a European trip that included a meeting with Pope John Paul II.
Some residents estimated the crowd, which lined the road on the six km (3.7 mile) route from the airport to Dili's cathedral, at more than 30,000 when Belo arrived home on a regular flight.
"It's bigger than the crowd for the blessing of the statue of Christ last month," one Dili resident who travelled to the airport told Reuters.
Around 20,000 people joined the blessing ceremony of the Christ the King statue outside Dili late last month.
"People had come down from the mountains in cars that were full of people with every seat taken and people on the roofs of the vehicles," the resident said.
"Many of them had travelled from outside of town and had begun arriving last night," another resident added.

Belo's car was driven slowly to the Cathedral, with a police escort, as people shouted from the sides of the road "Viva Bishop Belo, winner of the Nobel Peace Prize". He was due to say Mass later on Tuesday afternoon.
Riot police were not present despite the large crowd.

Belo is the most popular local figure in the former Portuguese colony. His often strong stand against human rights abuses since the 1975 Indonesian invasion has earned him deep respect in the majority Catholic territory.

Indonesia, which is mostly Moslem, unilaterally declared East Timor its 27th province in July 1976, the year after the invasion. The act was not recognised by the United Nations which still regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.
World attention was refocused on East Timor in October this year when Belo jointly won the Nobel prize with self-exiled East Timorese independence activist Jose Ramos Horta.
